quiz.explanation: Elasticity below 1.0 means demand is INELASTIC — it changes less than proportionally to price. This signals room to raise prices without significant demand loss. Above 1.0 = elastic (price-sensitive).

quiz.question: What does Net Revenue Retention (NRR) above 110% indicate?
options: Existing customers are spending more over time — your pricing supports natural expansion
You're acquiring 10% more customers each month
Your prices have increased by 10%
Customer satisfaction is above 110% of the benchmark
quiz.explanation: NRR above 110% means even without new customers, revenue from existing ones grows — through upgrades, expansion, and usage increases. This is the hallmark of well-designed pricing that grows with customer value.

lessons.title: Your 90-Day Pricing Optimisation Plan
lessons.subtitle: Everything you've learned, condensed into a practical 90-day action plan. Implement this and pricing becomes your competitive moat.

cards.headline: You now know more about pricing than 95% of business owners. The question isn't knowledge — it's implementation. This lesson gives you the system.
cards.body: Over 20 lessons, you've built a complete pricing toolkit: psychology, research, strategies, models, and metrics. But knowledge without action is worthless. Today you'll build your personal 90-day pricing optimisation plan — the system that turns everything you've learned into measurable profit.

cards.headline: Days 1–30: Foundation & Research
cards.body: Week 1: Audit current pricing against the 7 mistakes (Lesson 7). Score yourself honestly. Week 2: Run Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger research on your target segment (Lesson 5). Get real WTP data. Week 3: Map your customer segments and their different WTPs (Lesson 4). Identify your premium segment. Week 4: Define your pricing strategy (penetration, skim, or value-based) and validate it fits your business model (Lesson 6). Deliverable: a one-page "Pricing Position" document — your strategy, target segments, and WTP ranges.

cards.headline: Days 31–60: Architecture & Design
cards.body: Week 5: Design your tier structure — Good/Better/Best with clear value differentiation (Lesson 10). Week 6: Build your price communication — anchor, frame, present using the conversion stack (Lessons 14 & 19). Week 7: Set up your pricing metrics dashboard — ARPU, realisation, NRR, tier distribution (Lesson 20). Week 8: Plan your first price increase or restructure — strategy, communication, timeline (Lesson 15). Deliverable: new pricing page/proposal ready to launch, metrics dashboard tracking.

cards.headline: Days 61–90: Launch & Optimise
cards.body: Week 9: Launch new pricing to new customers (grandfather existing if needed). Week 10: Monitor metrics daily — watch conversion, churn, ARPU. Week 11: Run your first A/B test — try two different price frames or tier structures on split traffic. Week 12: Review results. Adjust based on data. Schedule your next quarterly pricing review. Deliverable: live new pricing, first month of data, documented learnings. Then repeat this cycle quarterly — pricing is never "done," it's a continuous optimisation loop.

cards.headline: Try It: Commit to Your First Action
cards.body: Choose ONE action to take this week: □ Run a Van Westendorp survey with 5 target customers. □ Audit your current price against the 7 mistakes. □ Draft a Good/Better/Best tier structure. □ Calculate your ARPU and price realisation. □ Design a price increase communication. Pick the one that feels most impactful for your business right now. Block 30 minutes in your calendar this week. Small action → big results. Congratulations — you've completed Pricing & Monetisation Mastery.

quiz.question: What should be the primary deliverable from the first 30 days of pricing optimisation?
options: A one-page "Pricing Position" document with your strategy, target segments, and WTP ranges
A completely new pricing page live on your website
A full competitive analysis of every competitor's pricing
Three months of pricing metrics data
quiz.explanation: The first 30 days are about research and clarity — understanding your position, your customers' WTP, and your strategic direction. Implementation comes in days 31–90 once the foundation is solid.

quiz.question: Once you've optimised your pricing, the work is done and you can move on to other priorities.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: Pricing is never "done" — it's a continuous optimisation loop. Markets shift, competitors change, customer value evolves. Schedule quarterly reviews to keep pricing aligned with current conditions.

quiz.question: What is the recommended approach when launching new pricing?
options: Launch to new customers first (grandfathering existing ones), monitor metrics, then A/B test and iterate
Change prices for all customers simultaneously without warning
Wait until you have perfect data before making any changes
Only change prices once per year regardless of what data shows
quiz.explanation: The safest launch approach: new customers get new pricing (zero churn risk), you monitor results, test variations, then gradually migrate existing customers with proper communication and notice.
